cell: safari-app · STATE matrix (Phase D states seat)
law: I-20 — webkit-engine (Playwright) and safari-app (safaridriver) are SEPARATE evidence cells. No webkit verdict below was copied into a safari verdict; every safariVerdict was measured in real Safari 26.4. Cells not run here are recorded UNREACHABLE-IN-CELL or UNVERIFIABLE-HERE, never green.
browser: Safari 26.4 (stock Cryptex build, AppleWebKit 605.1.15) on macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)
driver: safaridriver WebDriver classic @ http://localhost:4599, one session at a time, deleted on every path
origin: http://localhost:9000 — dev server UP, API-LESS (no mongo)

cells.webkitVerdict: dir=rtl applied post-load (MT-F022 #1 harness fix); overflowX 0; clipped list CAPPED AT 8 by states.mjs .slice(0,8) — true total unknown; the 8 named are spectrum-dot, an SVG path, and six katex MathML nodes
cells.safariVerdict: MEASURED — dir=rtl takes post-load in real Safari too; overflowX 0, overflowY 0; only TWO elements sit outside the viewport in the whole document: span.spectrum-dot.absolute and one SVG path
cells.note: PARTIAL INVERSION, and it is the katex half. WebKit-engine names six MathML nodes (math/semantics/mrow/msup/mi/mo) as outside the viewport; real Safari names NONE of them — Safari lays the visually-hidden .katex-mathml copy out inside its overflow:hidden parent. Neither is a product defect (the parent clips); the delta is an engine layout difference in hidden MathML. The two rows AGREE on the load-bearing facts: dir flips, overflowX is 0, RTL remains an UNCLAIMED capability rather than a broken one (MT-F022 consequence 4 re-derived in the safari-app cell).

cells.webkitVerdict: 8 clipped (CAPPED) — strip-row, strip-family, family-eyebrow, family-tiles, glass-chip, svg, path
cells.safariVerdict: MEASURED — 77 elements outside the viewport; the first 8 are spectrum-dot plus the SAME strip-row / strip-family / family-eyebrow / family-tiles / glass-chip / svg / path set
cells.note: AGREEMENT on the real signal: the gradient family-strip overhangs the viewport edge under RTL in BOTH cells. The count delta (8 vs 77) is NOT an inversion — the webkit harness truncates its list at 8, so its total was never measured. Any comparison of these numbers is a category error.
Effective agreement; the single delta is the spectrum-dot, which real Safari places one pixel past the edge on every RTL route (it is the ONLY offender on 4 of 5 RTL routes).
AGREEMENT, exactly, including the identity of the offender.

cells.webkitVerdict: After 12 Tabs focus NEVER LEAVES body; focusRingVisible null — MT-F022 #3 attributed this to macOS Full Keyboard Access being off in Playwright WebKit
cells.safariVerdict: MEASURED — after 12 Tabs focus is on main>…>div:nth-child(10)>div:nth-child(1) with focusRingVisible TRUE
cells.note: THE INVERSION, and it is MT-F022 #3 resolved from the other side. The safari-app cell traverses to a real, ring-bearing stop where webkit-engine sat on body. MT-F022's rule ('a WebKit-only gap is presumed Full-Keyboard-Access until Chromium agrees') is confirmed: the real browser agrees with Chromium, not with Playwright WebKit. NO keyboard defect may be booked from the webkit rows of this matrix.

A ring claim needs a per-stop, DOM-path-keyed walk in the safari-app cell (the kbd-reach.mjs shape), which this cell did not run.

cells.webkitVerdict: NOT IN THE WEBKIT MATRIX — states.mjs never ran a dark arm
cells.safariVerdict: MEASURED via the app's OWN toggle, not media emulation: localStorage['vueuse-color-scheme'] drives demo/color-picker/index.html:169-172, which puts class='dark' on <html>. dark -> htmlClass 'dark', body rgb(38,0,27); forced 'light' -> htmlClass '', body rgb(179,114,144). Both directions confirmed, same textLen 874 and same clipped set.
cells.note: REACHABLE-IN-CELL because the app persists its own scheme; no prefers-color-scheme emulation was needed or used. IMPORTANT CONFOUND FOR THE WHOLE MATRIX: this machine prefers dark, so the DEFAULT boot is dark — the rtl-desktop and keyboard-focus-desktop safari rows above were measured in DARK, while the webkit rows they sit beside were measured in Playwright's default LIGHT. None of the compared quantities (dir, overflowX, textLen, focus, clipped identity) is scheme-dependent, but the confound is declared rather than hidden. The zoom-200 and rtl-mobile rows were measured in LIGHT and are scheme-matched.

cells.webkitVerdict: NOT COMPARABLE — the webkit harness caps its list at 8
cells.safariVerdict: MEASURED and RUN TO GROUND rather than booked
cells.note: AN MT-F022-CLASS FALSE SIGNAL CAUGHT IN MY OWN HANDS. 694 of 1560 visible elements report right>clientWidth, which reads as a catastrophe and is not one: only 9 are ROOTS, and one root carries 1454 descendants. That root is div.glass-resting.card inside div.pane-wrapper--right at left=1280 right=1817 (377 CSS px past a 1440 viewport, parent overflow visible, document overflowX 0 so it cannot be scrolled to). The other 8 roots are katex-mathml nodes and one SVG path, all inside overflow:hidden parents — probe false positives. So the honest statement is ONE overhanging right-pane card, not 694 clipped elements. Under dir=rtl the same page reports 2, because the pane flips to the other edge. Whether the overhang is a defect belongs to the layout seat; this cell records the measurement and its mechanism.

unreachableInCell.reduced-motion-desktop (5 webkit rows): UNREACHABLE-IN-CELL. prefers-reduced-motion is a macOS System Settings switch; WebDriver classic has no media emulation and safaridriver exposes no override. MT-F022 #2's rAF finding CANNOT be re-derived in the safari-app cell — and see the rAF blind spot below, which would defeat it even if the media query could be set.
unreachableInCell.forced-colors-desktop (5 webkit rows): UNREACHABLE-IN-CELL. Increase Contrast / forced-colors is a system setting with no WebDriver hook. (states.mjs:8 already records that WebKit ignores Playwright's forcedColors, so those 5 webkit rows assert nothing either.)
unreachableInCell.pointer:coarse / prefers-color-scheme vi: UNREACHABLE-IN-CELL as media state. Dark was reached through the APP's own persisted toggle instead (see the dark-desktop cell); coarse pointer was not reached at all.

declaredBlindSpots.rAF / motion rate: UNMEASURABLE-IN-CELL. The safaridriver automation window reports document.visibilityState 'hidden' and document.hasFocus() false even after raising it with AppleScript (index->1 + activate), so WebKit throttles requestAnimationFrame to ~1 Hz: my own rAF chain ticked ONCE in 1500 ms, and the 16 ms setInterval sampler produced 6-7 samples across ~60 s. Every rafPer1500ms in my rows therefore reads 0 and MEANS NOTHING ABOUT THE APP. It is recorded as a blind spot, not as 'the app has no motion'. document.getAnimations() still returns 19-31 running CSS animations per route, which is measurable and is reported.
declaredBlindSpots.console / page errors: WebDriver classic cannot inject before load; window.onerror + unhandledrejection were installed AFTER load and after a forced reload. All 15 rows show an empty post-install error array. That is NOT a claim of zero boot errors.
declaredBlindSpots.window screenshots: BROKEN IN THIS CELL, and it now reproduces at DESKTOP size, widening the prior seat's finding. GET /session/<id>/screenshot at 1440x900 returned a pure-black 2880x1696 PNG, byte-identical across two different routes and two different colour schemes (sha256 592299a3b4b3cf2e55eb855f4ad350c8427c3e1367f7dd3a019c170203f658c8). The prior seat saw this only at 3440x1440. MECHANISM, now identified: the automation window is not visible (visibilityState hidden), so there is no window surface to capture — the same fact that throttles rAF. ELEMENT snapshots are unaffected and paint real content (dock-morph-safari26.4-element.png, 928x122, the dock rendered correctly). The two black frames are preserved as rtl-desktop-picker-1440-windowsnap-black.png and dark-desktop-picker-1440-windowsnap-black.png.
declaredBlindSpots.clipped-count comparability: states.mjs truncates its clipped list with .slice(0,8), so no webkit row states a total. My clippedTotal has no webkit counterpart; only the first-8 IDENTITIES are comparable.

morphArm.verdict: NOT-DRIVEN — and the reason is the cell, not the app
morphArm.whatDrivesExpansion: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:133 renders <GlassDock :collapse-delay="5000" :start-collapsed="false" :fit-content="true" :always-expanded="!isDesktop">. Posture is glass-ui useDockState's three-state FSM (collapsed|hover|pinned) driven by mouseenter / mouseleave+timer / click-on-collapsed, plus the consumer's ref-counted keepOpen()/release() hold (Dock.vue:86-88) and expand() on edit (Dock.vue:90). The morph itself is useDockMorphOrchestrator projecting the face onto the shared --dock-morph-t spring; morph.css then sets --dock-expand-t := --dock-morph-t under [data-morphing] and feeds it to the nested color-mix on .dock-plate background.
morphArm.howIDroveIt: Dispatched real DOM events (pointerover/enter/move + mouseover/enter/move, and the leave/out pair, and a full pointerdown/up + click on the collapsed dock) via execute/sync, because they are exactly what useDockState listens to. WebDriver pointer ACTIONS were tried first and HUNG the driver indefinitely (see limitations), so they were abandoned.
morphArm.whatHappened: The FSM ran: the dock left .expanded (--dock-expand-t 1, width 464-469) and entered .collapsed[data-morphing] (--dock-expand-t 'calc(1 - 0)', width 56 observed once), then returned. But --dock-morph-t stayed EXACTLY 0 in every single sample across 4+3 storm passes, the width never took an intermediate value, and the sampler captured 6-7 frames in ~60 s. The spring is rAF-driven and rAF is throttled to 1 Hz in a hidden window, so --dock-expand-t never traversed (0,1) and the nested color-mix was never resolved at a fractional t by the morph. Zero frames of genuine morph were driven; SURVIVED would be a false green.
morphArm.supplementarySyntheticSweep: Labelled synthetic, NOT the morph: with data-morphing forced on, --dock-expand-t was written across 246 fractional values (6 passes x 41 steps, both directions) while reading .dock-plate's resolved backgroundColor and borderColor each step. Every value resolved cleanly (e.g. t=0 -> color(srgb 0.384505 0.327291 0.27789 / 0.4544), t=1 -> color(srgb 0.390253 0.334104 0.290184 / 0.5776)); no throw, no crash, Safari alive. This exercises the STYLE-RESOLUTION path of the nested color-mix — which is precisely where the known crash signature aborts — but it cannot exercise paint, because the window does not render.
morphArm.safariSurvived: Safari 26.4 did not crash: sessions stayed alive and were deleted cleanly on every run, and NO Safari .ips was written at any point.
morphArm.crashReportsObserved: TWO crash reports of the EXACT glass-S0 signature exist on this machine today — and BOTH are webkit-engine, NOT safari-app, so neither is my cell's result and neither may be attributed to this arm: com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.Development-2026-07-27-111524.ips and -131147.ips. Both are the Playwright-bundled WebKit (procPath /Users/USER/Library/Caches/*/com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.Development, coalitionName com.microsoft.VSCode, parentProc launchd), both SIGABRT (Abort trap: 6) about 1.2-1.7 s after process launch.
morphArm.whatTheStackEstablishes: The crash class aborts inside toStyleColor(CSS::ColorMix) while the style builder applies BACKGROUND-COLOR during Document::resolveStyle — i.e. at STYLE RESOLUTION, not at paint, and on the very property morph.css nests color-mix into (.dock-plate background). That is the strongest available corroboration that --dock-expand-t through a nested color-mix background is the mechanism. It also means the arm does NOT require a visible window in principle — which makes the safari-app non-repro meaningful only as far as it goes: real Safari 26.4 resolved 246 fractional nested-color-mix backgrounds without aborting, while the Playwright WebKit build (625.1.21+) carries a signature that aborts on exactly that path.
morphArm.whatWouldFinishThisArm: A safari-app run in a VISIBLE, focused Safari window (visibilityState 'visible', rAF >= 20 Hz) so the spring actually traverses (0,1) and the page paints; everything else is already wired and reproducible from the scripts named below.

cellLimitations.webdriver-pointer-actions: POST /session/<id>/actions with a pointerMove HUNG safaridriver indefinitely (no response in 25 min; the session's whole command queue blocked, DELETE included, so create-session returned 'already paired' for both drivers on :4599 and :4622). Recovery was minimal and non-destructive: the automation window alone was closed by URL match (osascript, every document whose URL starts with http://localhost:9000), leaving the user's two Safari windows and every process untouched; the driver freed immediately. KEY actions (Tab) work normally — the 12-Tab walks above used them. Any later seat should drive pointers by dispatched DOM events, not by the actions endpoint.
cellLimitations.hidden-window: Every attempt to make the automation window visible failed (osascript 'set index of window to 1' + 'activate'): visibilityState stayed 'hidden', hasFocus false, rAF 1 Hz. This bounds the motion, paint and morph arms of the entire safari-app cell.
